_readme: Manual answers for films the matcher can't resolve on its own.
Keys are the normalized title: lowercase, no accents, no punctuation.
When a film comes out UNRESOLVED, its film_id in data/films.json is
exactly the key to use here.
Find the film on themoviedb.org and take the number from its URL:
tmdb_id   force this TMDb film, skipping the matcher entirely
csfd_url  use this exact CSFD page instead of a search link
skip      true = ignore this title completely (not a film, e.g. an event)

mouchy._comment: Fernando Eimbcke's 'Moscas' (2026). TMDb has no Czech title for it at all, so no title search can find it - this needs a manual id. Verified: director and 99min runtime both match Aero's listing.

me 20 stoleti._comment: Ildiko Enyedi's 'My Twentieth Century' / 'Az en XX. szazadom' (1989). TMDb has no Czech title, and searching the English translation of the Czech title doesn't hit the actual English release title either. Verified: director Ildiko Enyedi matches Aero's listing exactly.

mumbo jumbo._comment: Danish animated film, TMDb title 'When Mumbo Jumbo Grew Giant' (orig. 'Da Mumbo Jumbo blev kaempestor', 2026) - Bio Oko lists it under a shortened Czech title that happens to collide with several unrelated films also called 'Mumbo Jumbo'. TMDb's own title search never surfaces this candidate at all, so no threshold tuning would have found it. Verified: director Karsten Kiilerich and 83min runtime both match Bio Oko's listing exactly.

horke svatky._comment: 'Horke svatky' is a Czech translation of the title, not the distribution title TMDb knows - the real film is Almodovar's 'Bitter Christmas' (orig. 'Amarga Navidad', 2026). Found by searching the director's filmography. Verified: director Pedro Almodovar and runtime (111 scraped vs 112 on TMDb, normal rounding) both match Bio Oko's listing.

ztracena listina._comment: 'Ztracena listina' (Czech for 'The Lost Letter') is a translated title, not TMDb's distribution title - the real film is 'The Lost Letter' (orig. Ukrainian 'Propala hramota', 1972). Found by searching the director's filmography. Verified: director Borys Ivchenko and 79min runtime both match Bio Oko's listing exactly.

co nam zbylo z lasky._comment: Kino Pilotu doesn't expose director/runtime at all (see the scraper's module docstring - no JSON-LD on that site), so there is no independent signal to verify against here, unlike the other overrides in this file. Added anyway because it's the sole TMDb candidate and a precise semantic match: 'Co nam zbylo z lasky' (what's left of us, of love) is a literal translation of 'The Love That Remains' / 'Astin sem eftir er' (2025, Hlynur Palmason, a real Cannes-selected film that fits this cinema's programming exactly).

mrzuta rybka._comment: Same situation as 'co nam zbylo z lasky' - no verification signal available from Kino Pilotu's scraper. Sole candidate, and 'Mrzuta rybka' (grumpy/pouting little fish) is an exact thematic translation of 'The Pout-Pout Fish' (2026), a children's book adaptation - fits the kids'-film slot alongside this cinema's other family titles (Zootropolis 2, Toy Story 5, Moana).

sepot lesa._comment: No verification signal available (see above). TMDb has no Czech title or synopsis for this one at all. 'Sepot lesa' (whisper of the forest) matches 'Whispering Forest' (2025, orig. French-titled documentary about the Bialowieza primeval forest) - a 63-minute nature documentary, exactly the theme the Czech title describes.

120 bpm._comment: Edison Filmhub's own shortened Czech distribution title for '120 battements par minute' / 'BPM (Beats per Minute)' (2017) - a well-known Cannes Grand Prix winner. Single unambiguous title match; Edison gives no director/runtime to independently verify against.

lak na vlasy._comment: 'Lak na vlasy' is a literal Czech translation of 'Hairspray' (1988), not the distribution title TMDb indexes. Single unambiguous candidate, exact semantic match; no verification signal available from Edison's scraper.

noc 1961._comment: Antonioni's 'La Notte' (1961), screened by Kino Aero as 'Noc (1961)'. The bare trailing year is now stripped before searching (strip_year_suffix in tmdb.py, added after the 2026-07-30 audit), which fixed the sibling cases 'Kanaly (1957)' and 'Aladin (1992)' outright - but not this one: 'Noc' alone is a single very common Czech word, TMDb returns 20 unrelated matches and none scores above the 0.75 threshold. A genuine case for a manual id rather than any threshold change. Aero publishes no director/runtime for it, so verification is by title semantics: 'Noc' is the standard Czech title for La Notte, and it fits Aero's classics programming.
